policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'shall live' is compatible with both the qere conjunction plus perfect form and the ketiv imperfect form; no mapped textual note distinguishes them.
ASV reads indefinite 'rags and worn-out garments,' distinguishing qere סְחָבוֹת from ketiv הַסְּחָבוֹת ('the rags').
ASV 'As Jehovah liveth, that made us this soul' supplies no English counterpart that distinguishes omission from the ketiv object marker את; no mapped textual note decides the unit.
